$comment: The repository's record of what has been applied to PRODUCTION (travel-buddy, ajrurzioarfkagpuxfnb), taken from its supabase_migrations.schema_migrations. COMMIT AN ENTRY HERE IN THE SAME CHANGE THAT APPLIES THE MIGRATION. checkFlagSchemaPrerequisites compares the newest version here against the snapshot's productionMigrationWatermark and FAILS when this file is ahead -- that is how a stale snapshot is caught OFFLINE, with no live database access. Production DOES now have a schema_migration_ledger (created 2026-09-15) but it is not an inventory either -- it only carries rows for migrations applied through the ledger discipline, and the 2026-09-16 capture found three migrations applied to production at 07:56 UTC that wrote supabase_migrations rows and NO ledger row, plus five applied by us that wrote ledger rows and NO supabase_migrations row. Neither table is complete on its own, and migrations applied by hand through the Supabase dashboard write no row into supabase_migrations, so this file is necessarily a record of what WE applied, not proof of everything that is applied. It is a staleness tripwire, not an inventory. VERSIONS FOR MANUAL APPLIES: the five 2026-09-16 entries ran through execute_sql inside BEGIN/COMMIT with postcondition DO blocks, which writes a schema_migration_ledger row but not a supabase_migrations row, so their version strings here are their ledger applied_at instants rendered in the same YYYYMMDDHHMMSS shape -- derived from the database's own record of when they landed, not invented. 2026-09-16 AFTERNOON, three more entries, and their versions are LEDGER instants for the reason stated above: 2202_map_telemetry and 2222_map_telemetry_refusal_event both at 20260916141105 (one transaction -- 2222 amends 2202's payload guard, so they were applied together and share an applied_at), and 2256_media_intent_signals at 20260916151321. All three had CI ledger rows and no production table: 2202 carried a 'backfill' ledger row on production, which asserts only that the FILENAME existed when 2254 ran and never that the file ran, and 2256 carried no production row of any kind. The snapshot was refreshed in this same change to snapshots/20260916b-production-schema.json, so this file is not ahead of the capture. 2026-09-16 15:42, the port's FOUR-migration production apply set, applied from merged main 98fac66fc after the prerequisite counts were re-read and matched the runbook exactly (18/6/9/17/8/0/0) and the second writer was confirmed not to have moved. All four share the version 20260916154223, the ledger applied_at of the last of them: they ran as four separate transactions inside one minute and the ledger resolves to the second, so a shared version here is the honest rendering rather than four invented distinct instants. The snapshot was refreshed in the same change to snapshots/20260916c-production-schema.json, so this file is not ahead of the capture. 2026-09-16 17:37-17:42, FOUR more entries on two explicit owner decisions. 2470 completes MEDIA_CANONICAL (ORDER B: the flag was already TRUE and is untouched). 2315 + 2340 + 2480 stand up Sensing under SENSING_AUTH_POSTURE = anonymous_capable, Option B STAGED. 2481 is NOT listed and must never be applied under this posture: its CHECK makes attested- and unattested-device sessions unrepresentable. portava-ci still carries 2481 from an earlier Option A rehearsal, so CI and production genuinely differ here and CI is the one that is wrong for this posture. The snapshot was refreshed in the same change to snapshots/20260916d-production-schema.json, so this file is not ahead of the capture. 2026-09-16 20:13 - 2026-09-17 03:10, the TRIPS CHAIN: 41 further entries, every one a manual apply through execute_sql inside BEGIN/COMMIT with its own preconditions and postconditions, so their versions here are again their schema_migration_ledger applied_at instants in YYYYMMDDHHMMSS. Three pairs share a version because they shared a transaction minute and the ledger resolves to the second (2788/2790 at 20260916205754; 2789/2791/2792 at 20260916205844) -- a shared version is the honest rendering, not an invented distinct one. 2796 is NOT a spec migration: it repairs a latent privilege defect in 2784, whose booking-history trigger was not SECURITY DEFINER and so could never reach its own owner policies. This file was ahead of the capture between 2026-09-16 20:13 and this change, which is precisely the state checkFlagSchemaPrerequisites exists to refuse; snapshots/20260917-production-schema.json was captured in the same change and the pointer in snapshots/current.js moved with it. 2797/2798/2799 (recurring commitments) are NOT listed: they are rehearsed on portava-ci and have NOT been applied to production. 2026-09-20 19:46 - 19:56, FIVE entries that are a BACKFILL and are labelled one rather than presented as fresh work: 2996, 2997, 2800, 2840 and 2910 were applied to production that evening by someone other than this session, and NONE of them was recorded here. That is exactly the state this file exists to refuse, and the tripwire stayed silent through it for a reason worth writing down -- the tripwire only fires when this file is AHEAD of the snapshot, so a file that LAGS reality is invisible to it. The staleness was found by capturing production's table list and diffing it against baseline/20260917_production_tables.txt, which showed six tables (the 2910 Trails block) that no entry here accounted for. All five versions are their schema_migration_ledger applied_at instants, read from production, in the same YYYYMMDDHHMMSS shape as every manual apply above; 2800 and 2840 share 20260920195237 because they shared a transaction minute. A SIXTH object landed that evening, dead_check_vocabularies_2298, which wrote a supabase_migrations row and NO ledger row and corresponds to no file in src/migrations/; it is deliberately NOT listed, because inventing an entry for something this repository cannot name would be worse than the gap. 2026-09-21 07:52, TWO entries that ARE this session's work: 2963_memory_projector_place_lane_union and 2964_map_telemetry_disabled_discards, applied to production from merged main fd0b3a6f4 after both had been applied and certified on portava-ci by the merge of PR #511. They share the version 20260921075225 because their two ledger rows were inserted in one statement and the ledger resolves to the second. Both were applied through the Supabase Management API, which writes a supabase_migrations row (20260921074207 and 20260921074302); the LEDGER instant is used here anyway, because that is the convention every manual entry above follows and mixing two clocks in one column is how a version string stops meaning anything. snapshots/20260921-production-schema.json was captured in this same change, so this file is not ahead of the capture.
